subject: Larchmont: post-export session deletion, keystore & evidence request
messages:
From: Emily Jenkins <emily.jenkins@larchmonthealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sam Patel <sam.patel@larchmonthealth.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-export deletion & keystore audit (SOC 2 / SIG follow-up)

Rafael,

Thanks for the demo last week — good context. Two follow-ups from our security/compliance team as we scope the pilot:

1) Exported session artifacts: when Larchmont downloads session exports (e.g., for records or analytics), what is Redwood's policy for purging any server-side copies of those exported blobs? We need a clear timeline/process describing if/when exports are retained server-side and how you certify deletion.

2) Keystore-backed cache: our legal team is concerned about derived artifacts stored in your KV cache that are encrypted via a customer-scoped keystore. If a customer requests deletion of exported sessions, do you also rotate/expire relevant cache keys and provide proof that cached tokens/values were removed?

3) Evidence: for SIG/CAIQ mapping we need an attestation and preferably a small evidence bundle (logs showing deletion operations, keystore rotation entries, and a CSV manifest of deleted object ids/hashes). Can you provide a draft attestation and the supporting artifacts?

Can you loop in security for detailed answers and let us know an ETA?

Thanks,
Emily Jenkins
Security Program Manager
Larchmont Health

[Attachment: export_sample_example.json]

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Jenkins <emily.jenkins@larchmonthealth.com>
Cc: Sam Patel <sam.patel@larchmonthealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 12:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-export deletion & keystore audit (SOC 2 / SIG follow-up)

Emily — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; Kimberly and Jordan are on thread to provide the attestations and logs. We can produce a compact evidence bundle suitable for SIG/CAIQ review.

Summary (short):
- Server-side export copies: Redwood does not retain customer-initiated export blobs beyond the completion of the export pipeline unless a customer opts into server-side archival. By default exports are streamed to the requester and transient staging objects are deleted within 24 hours; we can reduce that for pilot customers to 0–1 hour on request.
- Keystore-backed cache: cache entries encrypted under a customer-scoped key are invalidated on deletion requests. We perform a key rotation and issue a deletion sweep for matching cache prefixes; rotation events and sweep results are logged in our keystore audit trail.
- Evidence: attaching a draft attestation and a small evidence pack with a redacted deletion manifest and keystore rotation log. If you need full hashes (sha256) we can include them under an encrypted artifact.

Immediate next steps: Kimberly, can you confirm the exact log fields we should pull for the CAIQ SIG supplement? Jordan, can you confirm if we can shorten the staging TTL to 1 hour for the Larchmont pilot and produce a deletion_manifest.csv with file ids and sha256 truncs?

Attachment: larchmont_evidence_pack_v2.zip (contains: deletion_manifest_sample.csv, keystore_rotation_log_20270405.csv, attestation_draft.md)

Cheers,
Rafael
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Emily Jenkins <emily.jenkins@larchmonthealth.com>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@larchmonthealth.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 10:18:00 -0400
Subject: INTERNAL: Larchmont evidence details and required artifacts

Kimberly / Jordan — internal note (please reply-all when ready). Below are the minimal items Emily requested and the extraction details. I included the customer-facing language I'll use so we stay aligned.

Requested artifacts (minimum):
- deletion_manifest.csv: columns = exported_object_id, exported_filename, deletion_timestamp_iso, sha256_trunc (first 12 chars), redaction_note. Redact any PII in filenames; provide mapping in the secure artifact container.
- keystore_rotation_log.csv: columns = rotation_id, key_id, rotation_timestamp_iso, rotated_by_service_account (redwood-keystore@redwoodinference.com), impacted_prefixes (comma-delimited).
- keystore_audit_logs: event-level logs for the rotation + sweep (we'll package a filtered slice covering 2027-04-05T00:00:00Z — 2027-04-08T00:00:00Z).
- attestation_draft.md: one-paragraph attestation signed by Security Ops that states scope, retention TTL (staging), and deletion/sweep confirmation methodology.

Technical notes:
- For the pilot we can set export staging TTL to 1 hour by flipping the export_ttl policy for Larchmont's tenant flag. That will cause the staging S3 objects to be lifecycle-deleted by our orchestrator and also trigger a background sweep to zero any in-memory cache references.
- The cache sweep is implemented as a prefix scan on the tenant's cache namespace; it enqueues tombstones and performs secure erasure of values, then rotates the keystore key material. The keystore rotation itself is an async operation with a rotation record emitted to the keystore audit stream.

Jordan: can you confirm the sweep will emit a deletion operation id for each object and whether we can include the operation id column in deletion_manifest.csv?
Kimberly: once Jordan confirms the data fields, can Security Ops produce the one-paragraph attestation and sign it? I will deliver to Emily and request DocuSign if needed.

Thanks — Rafael

From: Emily Jenkins <emily.jenkins@larchmonthealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@larchmonthealth.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 14:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-export deletion & keystore audit (SOC 2 / SIG follow-up)

Thanks, Rafael — this is helpful. A couple of clarifying asks before we mark the SIG evidence as complete:

- Deletion manifest: Larchmont legal prefers full sha256 hashes for chain-of-custody; if you can provide truncated hashes in the thread but place the full hashes inside an encrypted artifact (we'll provide a public key or use your KMS envelope), that will work.
- Operation ids: yes please include operation_id column (that maps to your internal deletion sweep records).
- Attestation: the one-paragraph signed attestation is sufficient. We'll need an executed DocuSign envelope from Security Ops that confirms the attestation language and scope (I linked a placeholder).

If you can deliver the encrypted artifact + signed attestation by Monday EOD we'll move forward with the pilot kickoff. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Emily
